subject: Drata renewal — options and Trust Center integration
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@drata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Drata renewal — options and Trust Center integration

Hi Samira,

We’re approaching the renewal window for our Drata subscription (contract ends 2027-05-15). Before we pull legal into a formal redline round, I want to surface a couple of options and get a firm sense on pricing and migration implication if we were to shift any controls to Trust Center tooling instead of using Drata for everything.

Context: Redwood plans to add a dedicated Private deployment offering later this year and Security wants an auditable path for the new environments. We’ve been happy with Drata’s integrations but need clarity on:
- 12 vs 24 month pricing tiers and any pro-rated credit for unused months
- Cost and timeline to support the Trust Center publishing/integration instead of Drata-hosted trust pages
- Any changes to evidence collection limits (api calls/hosted log retention) that would affect our infra cost

Can you:
1) Share a renewal quote for 12/24 months (break out seat/unit pricing and any marketplace discounts).
2) Confirm whether Drata will provide a migration/hand-off package for Trust Center migration and an estimated cost.
3) Point to any standard SOW or integration task list we should expect.

I attached a very rough SOW draft and a short internal checklist. Please send the quote as an attachment so I can route it to procurement. If possible, include a 14-day window for us to finalize terms — we may need a short extension while Legal runs redlines.

Thanks — Jonas

Attachments: sow_draft_jonas_20270403.docx (SOW draft, 2 pages)

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Samira Khan <samira@drata.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Drata Sales <sales@drata.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Drata renewal — options and Trust Center integration

Thanks for the note, Jonas — appreciate the detail. Quick answers up front, and I’ve attached a formal quote (see drata_quote_q2_2027.xlsx) plus a checklist for Trust Center hand-off.

Highlights:
- We can provide both 12- and 24-month renewal options. The 24-month comes with a 10% discount on subscription fees (standard).
- We offer a Trust Center integration package: it’s billed as a one-time integration fee (professional services) plus a light migration effort to export trust page content. Ballpark PS estimate: $8k–$12k depending on connector complexity.
- Evidence collection: current tier includes 100k API evidence events/month. If you expect higher throughput from Private/on-prem exports, we can bump that; pricing is linear per additional 25k events.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Sign the quote as-is to lock current pricing.
2) We can do a technical kickoff to scope the Trust Center export and finalize the PS estimate.

I’m attaching the quote and the integration checklist. If Procurement wants a short extension window, we can hold pricing for 14 calendar days from the date on the quote.

Best,
Samira

Attachments: drata_quote_q2_2027.xlsx (renewal quote), drata_trustcenter_checklist.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@drata.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Drata renewal — options and Trust Center integration

Samira — thanks for the quick turnaround.

I had our legal ops team skim the quote and the integration checklist. High-level requests we’ll need before signing:
- Addendum for data processing: confirm subprocessor list and include a commitment to notify us 30 days prior to any subprocessor changes.
- Liability cap: Drata’s standard limit is currently 1x ARR; we will likely negotiate this down to 0.5x for critical infra controls or carve out willful misconduct.
- SLA credit language: we need a clear SLA with uptime credits or an agreed escalation path.
- Evidence export/exportability: include a clause guaranteeing a machine-readable export of control evidence and logs for migration to third-party trust pages (Trust Center) and state the export format/retention windows.

I attached redlines (redlines_law_20270405.pdf) with comments on data residency and deletion timelines. Also note procurement wants the breakout by license type in the quote (user seats vs managed connectors).

Two asks for you, Jonas:
1) Can Procurement (Marcus) confirm whether we want a 12- or 24-month term? My recommendation is 24 for stability if the pricing delta is favorable.
2) Marcus — can you run a quick cost projection for the PS work + incremental event costs vs a short Trust Center pilot? I want to see 6- and 12-month TCO.

Thanks — Laura

Attachments: redlines_law_20270405.pdf (legal redlines, 3 pages)

--
Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@drata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Drata renewal — options and Trust Center integration

Samira — thanks, all, for the details. Quick confirmation and next steps: 

- We’d like to proceed with a 24-month renewal pending the contract revisions Laura proposed. Marcus is running the TCO and should have numbers by EOD Friday.
- Can you confirm Drata’s willingness to accept the two-week signature window and to start a technical scoping call next week? Laura’s redlines are attached to this thread; please flag anything you can’t accept so we can route quickly.
- If Drata can provide a modest credit on the PS package (even $2k) to help offset the migration evaluation, that would make the economics much easier to justify for Product.

Proposed meeting: Thurs 2027-04-08 10:00am PT — 30 minutes — technical scoping + procurement alignment. Samira, does that work? If not, offer two alternatives.

Thanks,
Jonas
